name: Maha Shivratri
description: The Great Night of Lord Shiva, celebrating the solemn festival of devotion, meditation, and spiritual awakening.

name: Holi
description: The vibrant Festival of Colors celebrating the victory of good over evil and the arrival of spring.

name: Rama Navami
description: Celebration of the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu.

name: Hanuman Jayanti
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Hanuman, the symbol of selfless devotion, strength, and courage.

name: Akshaya Tritiya
description: A highly auspicious day symbolizing never-diminishing good fortune, prosperity, and spiritual merit.

name: Guru Purnima
description: Honoring spiritual and academic gurus and celebrating Maharishi Veda Vyasa.

name: Raksha Bandhan
description: Celebrates the sacred bond of protection and love between brothers and sisters.

name: Krishna Janmashtami
description: The auspicious birth anniversary of Lord Krishna, the divine speaker of the Bhagavad Gita.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Grand festival celebrating the arrival of Lord Ganesha, remover of obstacles.

name: Sharad Navratri Begins
description: Nine divine nights dedicated to worshipping Goddess Durga and her nine sacred forms (Navadurga).

name: Dussehra (Vijayadashami)
description: Celebrates the victory of Lord Rama over Ravana and Goddess Durga over Mahishasura.

name: Diwali (Deepavali)
description: The grand Festival of Lights celebrating righteousness, prosperity, and Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya.

name: Ekadashi Vrat
description: Sacred twice-monthly fast observed on the 11th tithi of Shukla and Krishna paksha dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

name: Pradosham Vrat
description: Bi-monthly twilight fast observed on the 13th tithi dedicated to Lord Shiva and Parvati.

name: Sankashti Chaturthi
description: Monthly moonrise fast dedicated to Lord Ganesha for removing difficulties and obstacles.

name: Purnima (Full Moon)
description: Auspicious full moon day ideal for Satyanarayan Puja, fasting, and spiritual reflection.

name: Amavasya (New Moon)
description: New moon day dedicated to ancestral rites (Pitr Tarpana) and inner reflection.
